articles.title: Attack on Titan 3: The Final Preview
articles.summary: Attack on Titan 3 may come with a number, but it isn’t a direct sequel in the truest sense of the word. It’s more of a retelling.  Based on my time with it, Attack on Titan 3 is juggling a lot of plates, and its ambition to do something new with the franchise is pretty laudable.
articles.body:
This isn’t a straight retelling of the anime, but it does follow the same overall storyline.

The designers aim to include something in combat for more advanced/experienced players too.

The moments in-between big battles are some of my favorites so far.

I must confess something before I get this preview started: I bowed out of Attack on Titan early. After the first season, actually. I didn’t think it was terrible or anything. I was there for the human drama. Little people swinging around like Spider-Man and dealing with their trauma while playing a game of David and Goliath against big, scary Titans. But when those little dudes started being able to become Titans, well… it just wasn’t for me. But after spending some time with Attack on Titan 3 and speaking to producer Hideo Suzuki, I’m tempted to give it another go… at least as a video game.

Attack on Titan 3 may come with a number, but it isn’t a direct sequel in the truest sense of the word. It’s more of a retelling. Part of that, Suzuki told me, was because it’s been seven years since Attack on Titan 2: Final Battle. “Right after the previous game, we already had started talking about the sequel, but at the time the anime series was still ongoing. So we were like, ‘What kind of concept should [the next one] be?’ And we did think about just covering the new parts of the anime series, but as a game or as a one product, we didn't think it was quite enough. So we were like, ‘Okay, one series is coming to an end, so why don't we just cover the story from beginning to the end and just kind of follow that storyline?’”

But Attack on Titan 3 isn’t just a straight retelling. You’ll be strapping on your ODM gear as an original character, but your backstory is interesting. After your squad is wiped out on your first mission as a squad leader, your character – I named mine John Titan, not knowing I could later choose their gender – is too traumatized (and afraid of fighting Titans) to continue. But since they also happen to be a great engineer and a generational talent with ODM gear, they’re kept on to fix things and train new recruits. It’s an interesting role to step into; games rarely ask you to embody deeply traumatized people who are so badly mentally broken that they have to step away from what they were great at.

Suzuki, however, told me that decision was intentional. “The reason that we had that kind of story in the beginning is we needed to establish that the Titans are the humans’ enemy. So the character goes to battle, he experiences the loss and trauma and then goes back with a stronger determination to fight Titans from then on. This time, the character is set up as a senior to Eren and other characters. And I mean, although he is a senior or more veteran trooper, if he's so strong from the beginning, there won't be much story to tell. So we have to have some kind of setback in the beginning for him to go through and it's that incident in the beginning. And then he's going to kind of play the role of Eren and others' mentor, but then they will work together and then they recover from the trauma and grow after.”

After playing with the character creator, I’m assigned to the 104th cadets, where I’ll be instructing Eren Jaeger, Armin Arlett, and Mikasa Ackerman, among others. My job, along with another hard-assed instructor named Keith, is to mold these kids into proper soldiers. But we have to break them first. You have to prepare the clay before you can shape it. But these recruits aren’t just blank slates. Like the show (and manga) it’s based on, Attack on Titan’s characters are their own people, sometimes to a fault. As soon as the initiation ceremony is over, Eren Jaeger bombards me with questions about why there aren’t more scouting missions and why we aren’t retaking the walls, and I’m forced to watch as my character relives their own shame. It’s a neat moment.

But I have to get to know these kids, too. Attack on Titan is probably most famous for its high-flying human vs. Titan battles or its knock down, drag out Titan-on-Titan brawls, but it’s a human story at heart, and building relationships with the other characters is a core part of Attack on Titan 3.

“There are many ways that the player can build a friendship with anime characters, and one of them is giving gifts to them,” Suzuki tells me later. “A second one is to eat together in a mess hall, and also they can invite those characters into their room and have conversations. So by pleasing the other characters, they can build rapport, a better friendship, and then it will affect the combat… These comrades that you build friendships with, you can invite them or you can take them onto these exterior missions or exterior scouts. And outside of the wall, you of course have battles against Titans and the player and those characters can work together to carry out special skills. We call these Buddy Arts… So the better relationship you have with these other characters… the better that your exterior missions or scouts are going to get.”

First, though, I have to whip them into fighting shape, and that means learning how to use the ODM gear. Grappling to rocks and trees before flinging yourself to the next place is a blast, and it feels like you have a lot of control over every aspect of movement. There are several features that are new to the series, like the ability to anchor yourself to buildings or trees, precisely control your altitude, or even slide under arches. When I asked him about redesigning the ODM gear, Suzuki told me that they wanted to make sure they were keeping pace with how games had evolved since Attack on Titan 2, but also offer something for more advanced players. “I think in the previous game, it was pretty playable for people who are not advanced game players, but in this one we wanted to have those advanced players to play better, battle better, and have a more sense of achievement when they defeat the Titans.

“But improving the ODM wasn’t enough,” Suzuki told me. The Titans have to improve with it because the team at Omega Force wanted those fights to feel suitably meaningful and epic. “In the previous game, the range of [ODM] control that you had was pretty narrow, and at the same time it was kind of simpler and easy for all players across the board. And this one, the base is still simple… but this time you had more control over a lot of the actions that you take and then you can really narrow down your tactics accordingly… but then that wasn't enough. If ODM only gets better, then the Titans are not going to be as threatening to the players. So we had to evolve the Titans as well. So their systems, for example, their algorithm and battle patterns, we definitely improved those too. And so they're still threatening Titans and they're big obstacles [for] the humans.”

I finally get my first crack at one after I jump to a later point in the story. I have to cleave through some human enemies, but they’re not too terrible, and it helps me get a feel for actual combat before taking on a Titan: the War Hammer Titan, to be exact, and it’s a bear of a fight. Unlike the Titan I fought earlier on in the game’s tutorial, I can’t damage it directly. Instead, I have to wear it down by filling up its Break Gauge before I can go in for the kill. Fighting efficiently means dodging and parrying attacks while getting my own licks in, but it’s more of a battle of patience than anything else. I’m like a mosquito fighting an elephant; I gotta take it down a bite at a time, and it’ll take them a lot less effort to squash me than it would for me to cause him meaningful harm.

Thankfully, I have the tools. I just have to manage them. Healing Tonics top me off when he smacks me around, new blades replace old ones when they dull and no longer make a dent, and Combat Arts deal more damage when I do enough damage to earn them. By far the coolest ones, though, are the Buddy Arts, which are flashy as hell. I feel slick every time I pull one off. Even with them, though, the fight is a matter of endurance. I almost make it, but I falter at the end. Not bad for a mosquito.

What I played of Attack on Titan 3’s battles felt memorable, but what stuck with me after my demo ended was all the time I spent out of combat with the other characters of this world. It makes the fights against the Titans hit harder than it would if they were happening all the time. “That was very much intentional,” Suzuki told me when I asked him about it. “This IP can be all battles. I mean, no one's going to complain about that, but because the anime characters are so attractive, they have so much depth. So to show their daily lives will probably make the fans happy… In manga and anime too, there are a lot of comical moments and events. So there's [a] tension-and-release kind of relationship. I think that makes the game more enjoyable.”

Suzuki told me that he hopes introducing a new character will help old fans see the story in a different way and introduce new players to Attack on Titan, but Attack on Titan 3 doesn’t just recreate the anime. There’s plenty of new stuff for them to discover, too. “We do have some original content as well, so we have a lot of sub stories and events. And we don't really say this out loud in interviews and stuff, but… we actually put so many of these sub-stories and events in this particular title and we work very closely with Kodansha, the IP holder. And so I want the players to enjoy every single bit of that.”

Suzuki also let drop one more detail for fans to look forward to as we wrapped up: "We've already announced that the opening anime sequence will be produced by Mappa. They're the creator of the anime. And this I have not said anywhere yet, but I watched the work in progress version of the opening movie and the quality is just phenomenal. So I really want the players to look forward to that.”

Based on my time with it, Attack on Titan 3 is juggling a lot of plates, and its ambition to do something new with the franchise is pretty laudable. Will it make me an Attack on Titan guy? Who knows? But I’d be lying if I said I wasn’t curious to put on my ODM gear one more time and help my character complete their quest for redemption. You can’t hide from the worst moments of your life, but you can choose how you face them, and who you face them with. Either way, you’ve got to learn to live with them, and fight your demons (and Titans) head on.

While you're here, check out these recent previews of other big upcoming games we've checked out recently!

Will Borger is an IGN freelancer. You can find him on Bluesky @edgarallanbro.

articles.title: Essential Combat Tips for Phantom Blade Zero - Phantom Blade Zero Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Being a master swordsman in Phantom Blade Zero takes more than just swinging your blade around and somersaulting every time someone takes a swing at you.
articles.body:
Being a master swordsman in Phantom Blade Zero takes more than just swinging your blade around and somersaulting every time someone takes a swing at you. There’s nuance to this, details that can make the difference between whether it's your head, or that of your opponents that goes rolling. That’s why we’ve put together these tips and tricks to help you master combat in Phantom Blade Zero.

Essential Combat Tips for Phantom Blade Zero

Years of action games like Ninja Gaiden or Dark Souls have taught players the value of dodging, blocking, and hitting back in the windows in between. However, that’s not typically the best approach here. Instead, most of your defense should come via parries.

That means timing button taps when attacks land, not holding it down and waiting. Not only does this keep you safe, it’s also often the best way to chip away at an enemy's sha-chi meter, breaking their guard and opening them up to attacks. For tougher enemies, especially bosses, this is your window to do meaningful damage. Ideally, you are looking for the flash of sparks that lets you know you’ve timed your parry perfectly.

Soul can carve through basic enemies without too much trouble. However, tougher baddies and bosses lie in wait to make his day much worse, and they won’t be impressed with a few basic attacks.

Really putting the hurt on them comes down to timing. Use your attacks and parries to break down the enemies guard first, go all out on the aggression. A particularly effective damage phase will look something like this: Guard is broken and you consume your Sha-Chi essence, then you empty your sha-chi meter with your Sha-Chi attacks, switch weapons, and use your now refilled sha-chi to do it again until the enemy stagger ends.

Fights against tough enemies, especially bosses, are as much about managing your sha-chi meter as they are about your quick-twitch combat skills. You need to keep your meter up, when it runs empty you are exposed to a lot of potential damage. Follow the 30% rule, as long as your Sha-chi is greater than 30%, swing freely, including using your sha-chi attacks. However, once it drops below that threshold, focus on just standard attacks until it refills. The exceptions are when you are pummeling a guard broken enemy like we mentioned before, or when you are about to switch weapons, which will instantly refill your sha-chi.

Always have one shieldbreaker phantom edge equipped

While Soul has an extensive arsenal, you only get to use four weapons, two standard and two phantom edges, in a single fight. Use whatever tools of destruction you like, no judgement here, but do yourself a favor and make sure to always have at least one Phantom Edge that specializes in breaking down shields. Shielded enemies will appear fairly regularly, and most standard weapons will take forever to break through their guard. But, if you have something like Dread Axe, or Iron Gauntlets equipped, you can smash through them almost instantly, saving a lot of time and effort against harder targets.

One of the early upgrades to Soul is called Flowing Chi. The description lists a bunch of requirements, but all you need to know is that this is unlimited free usage of your Phantom Edges , in the right context. Once you have this ability, you will start seeing a new button prompt appear. Tap it quick enough, and Soul will bust out an attack from a phantom edge, without consuming any Remnant Spark. When the prompt appears and what attack is used depends on the enemy, and whether or not you’ve unlocked the weapon used in the combo, but it can add a powerful effect to the middle of your assault. You can even get an item that grants a chance to generate new Remnant Spark anytime you use these free attacks.

Jagged Steel is a top tier weapon you get early, upgrade it right away

Early on you’ll face a boss called Jagged Steel, the Frenzied Brute . Cut him down to get his sword, also called Jagged Steel . You’ll unlock the ability to upgrade weapons soon, and make this your top priority; it’s by far one of the most powerful early-game weapons you can get your hands on. It has a great moveset, deals solid damage, and builds up a status effect called bleed, dealing a large chunk of additional damage when it procs. Get this to level five as soon as you can to unlock a special attack that builds bleep quickly on guard-broken enemies, and thank us later.

Another great weapon available in the early hours is the Scarlet Wraithblade. However, unlike Jagged Edge, this is on an optional boss, and completely missable. Don’t miss it. This massive two-handed sword cleaves through enemies quickly. It also leaves a wake of red lilies behind, which drain the sha-chi and health of any enemy standing in them, including bosses. Given how important draining sha-chi is to set up your attack opportunities, that’s a huge benefit.

To get the Scarlet Wraithblade, you’ll need to reach the Sha-chi tower in the Weeping Creek Valley, which you'll come across naturally as part of the story during Steel and Steam . After dealing with the monks on the first floor, look for an opening in the floor, slide down, and follow the path to the left to find Hua, Deadly Betrothed. You’ll need to beat her to get this sword. Be warned though, she’s no pushover. Check out our detailed Hua boss fight guide for help.

Soul gets access to a wide variety of accessories over his travels, and can eventually equip up to six of them at a time to maximize his combat potential. The game will often telegraph what sort of enemies you will be facing based on what accessories it drops, like giving you the Cavalrybane, right before you take on a particularly nasty jerk on horseback. As a general rule of thumb, if you get a new accessory specific to a type of enemy, or negating a type of damage, consider equipping it sooner rather than later.

Still, some accessories are good in almost any situation. Here are a few of our favorites.

The Token of Pursuit increases damage to Guard-Broken enemies. Since that’s when you’ll deal most of your damage, that’s an easy winner.

The Quick Hand Pendant and Quick Hand Might boost your damage with one and two-handed weapons respectively. That’s especially useful if you are doubling up on either weapon type.

The Mother’s Talisman restores some of your HP when your guard is broken. While we don’t suggest spending a lot of time in this state, if you are clever with your weapon switching, you can leverage this for some badly needed mid-fight healing.

The Reflex Device increases the timing window for your dodges and parries. Fully upgraded it gives a 25% boost. That’s a pretty big difference, and, with how much you’ll be using those moves, it can be a literal game changer with those tight windows.

It’s a dangerous world out there, but if you follow these tips you can turn the tables and become the danger yourself.

articles.title: How to Start the Charting the Unknown DLC (All Requirements) - Crimson Desert Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The first Crimson Desert DLC, Charting the Unknown, introduces several new questlines alongside shipbuilding that may have you wondering how to start them.
articles.body:
The first Crimson Desert DLC, Charting the Unknown, introduces several new questlines alongside shipbuilding that may have you wondering how to start them. We've included how far you'll need to get to get your first ship, how to continue the story of Kliff, Damiane, and Oongka, as well as plenty of other helpful info. Such as how to start the Garden of Trials as well!

How to Start the Shipbuilding and Ocean Questline

Before you can start sailing in Charting the Unknown, you'll need to progress the Greymanes Faction Quests . This requires completing the Gathered Will quest chain under Grounds of the Sunrise . The final quest you'll need to finish in that section is Expanding the Camp . Not to be confused with a previous quest of the same name under Embers of Return.

Upon completing the right one, you'll then have access to a new Greymanes Faction Quest category, Chartering the Unknown. This has a total of 14 quests, with three quest chains immediately available: A Wider World, Shield of Hernand, and Renewed Vitality. These will get you to owning your first small ship, until you can build or purchase a larger ship.

With that said, you'll need a lot of Camp Funds to get a bigger ship. For example, a large ship costs 6,000,000 Camp Funds.

To continue the main story and learn more about Kliff, Damiane, and Oongka, you'll need to complete the original main questline first . After finishing Epilogue: Journey's End and starting Crimson Desert with the DLC, Charting the Unknown, you'll have three new questlines available.

Make sure to play as the relevant character for each quest in the table below before trying to start them. Otherwise, you won't be able to work on that quest chain.

If you want to challenge yourself and experience the boss rush added in the Chartering the Unknown DLC, Garden of Trials, you'll need to finish the main story first. Fortunately, this doesn't require completing any of the Chartering the Unknown story quests previously mentioned. Once you've finished the questline in the original story, Epilogue: Journey's End, you'll be able to unlock it.

Make your way to the Axiom Archive in the Abyss , directly above the Town of Hernand. You'll also find it inside The Path of Providence when looking at the Abyss on your map. Travel there and then head toward the building straight ahead of the Abyss Nexus to trigger a cutscene.

Upon approaching the archive, a cutscene will trigger that transports you to the Garden of Trials. Continue forward, where you'll find many short pillars with cubes resting on them. You can then step on a pad near a trial to examine the cube there. As long as you've defeated these bosses previously, you'll be able to challenge them back-to-back without any consumables.

Up Next: Best Builds Guide: Weapons, Armor, and Abyss Gears

articles.title: Death Stranding Isolations Anime Gets First Trailer
articles.summary: Kojima Productions revealed the first trailer for Death Stranding Isolations, an original anime series set in the world of Death Stranding, scheduled to release on Disney+ next year.
articles.body:
Kojima Productions revealed the first trailer for Death Stranding Isolations, an original anime series set in the world of Death Stranding , scheduled to release on Disney+ next year.

The news was shared in a tweet late on October 29 (the morning of October 30 in Japan). In the trailer, a girl with blonde hair is roused from sleep by dreams of being consumed by the tar.

The tweet itself doesn't provide any more clarity; in the post, a quote reads, "My mom became a crater."

DEATH STRANDING ISOLATIONS Teaser Trailer & New Details Revealed! "My mom became a crater." An all-new animated series set in the world of DEATH STRANDING, featuring an original story driven by its own unique ensemble of characters. Streaming exclusively on Disney+ in 2027! Directed by Takayuki Sano Series Composition & Screenplay by Tow Ubukata Animated by E&H production #DeathStranding #DeathStrandingIsolations — KOJIMA PRODUCTIONS (Eng) (@KojiPro2015_EN) October 30, 2026

DEATH STRANDING ISOLATIONS Teaser Trailer & New Details Revealed! "My mom became a crater." An all-new animated series set in the world of DEATH STRANDING, featuring an original story driven by its own unique ensemble of characters. Streaming exclusively on Disney+ in 2027! Directed by Takayuki Sano Series Composition & Screenplay by Tow Ubukata Animated by E&H production #DeathStranding #DeathStrandingIsolations

Death Stranding Isolations is promised to be an original story driven by its "own unique ensemble of characters," suggesting that Sam Porter Bridges, Fragile, and co. won't be major players in the narrative.

As previously announced , the series will stream exclusively on Disney+ in 2027, though no exact date was given. The anime is directed by Takayuki Sano, known for doing the key animation, as well as designing creatures and props, directing, and many other duties for a swath of major anime over the years. Most notably, he served as the animation director for Attack on Titan's final season, as well as episodes of Jujutsu Kaisen and the movie Jujutsu Kaisen 0.

Tow Ubukata is set to write the series' screenplay. Ubukata is a noted science-fiction author who lent his talents to Psycho-Pass 3 and Psycho-Pass: Providence, Ghost in the Shell: The New Movie, and was the Free Scenario Plotter for Shenmue.

E&H production are animating the series, best known for their work on Undead Unluck: Winter Arc, Ninja Kamui, and the 2026 Magic Knight Rayearth reboot.

Kojima also unveiled a new poster for his upcoming horror game in collaboration with director Jordan Peele, OD Knock , showing Sophia Lillis looking up at a long, red object above her.

This is the latest news from Kojima after the game director expressed an intention to make cameos in films and TV, with an appearance in a "big" live-action film coming up. His studio's next big action espionage game, Physint, was also in the news recently after changing hands from Sony to Xbox . Thus far, details on this game are still sparse, but Kojima has confirmed a few cast members in Bill Skarsgard , Charlie Fraser and Minami Hamabe.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

articles.title: Valkyries most to blame for ugly WNBA Finals Game 6 loss vs. Dream
articles.summary: The Golden State Valkyries had an opportunity to secure their first WNBA championship Thursday afternoon. Instead, a disastrous first quarter put them in a h...
articles.body:
The Golden State Valkyries had an opportunity to secure their first WNBA championship Thursday afternoon. Instead, a disastrous first quarter put them in a hole they could never quite climb out of.

Golden State fell 80-69 to the Atlanta Dream in Game 6 of the WNBA Finals , setting up a winner-take-all Game 7 on Saturday in San Francisco. Despite a late comeback attempt, the Valkyries could not overcome a 20-point halftime deficit as Atlanta forced the series back to Golden State.

The Valkyries entered Thursday's matchup having won two consecutive games, but looked nothing like the team that had taken control of the series. Atlanta's offense came alive early, while Golden State struggled to generate much of anything on the other end.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

So who deserves the most blame for the Valkyries' missed opportunity to close out the WNBA Finals?

Golden State's biggest problem Thursday was apparent almost immediately. The Valkyries simply did not look prepared to match the intensity of an Atlanta team fighting to keep its championship hopes alive.

The Dream shot 11-of-15 from the field and 6-of-8 from beyond the arc in the opening quarter, building a commanding 32-15 advantage. Atlanta had already matched its entire first-half scoring output from Game 5 just six and a half minutes into Thursday's contest.

Some of that can be attributed to the Dream making difficult shots, but Golden State's defense also failed to establish the physicality that had been so important throughout its postseason run.

Valkyries head coach Natalie Nakase deserves some criticism for her team's slow start. Golden State was one win away from a championship, yet looked overwhelmed by Atlanta's aggressiveness on both ends of the floor.

The unusual 12:30 p.m. Thursday tipoff could have disrupted the teams' normal routines, but that is hardly an excuse. Both teams were dealing with the same circumstances, and Atlanta had no trouble finding its rhythm.

Golden State eventually made adjustments, particularly with its defensive pressure in the second half. But those changes came far too late.

Nakase has guided the Valkyries to within one win of a championship. Still, her team's inability to come out prepared for arguably its biggest game of the season deserves scrutiny.

Valkyries' defense had no answer for Atlanta's early shooting

Golden State's defense has been one of the biggest reasons for its success throughout the Finals. Unfortunately, that defensive identity was almost nonexistent during Thursday's opening quarter.

Allisha Gray finished with 23 points, while Rhyne Howard added 21 as Atlanta repeatedly capitalized on Golden State's defensive breakdowns. Angel Reese also added 15 points and 13 rebounds, giving the Dream another productive offensive option .

The Valkyries allowed Atlanta to score 46 points in the first half, a particularly disappointing showing considering the Dream had managed just 55 points in their Game 5 loss.

Veronica Burton acknowledged Golden State's defensive shortcomings following the game.

"They scored 32 points in the first quarter. That's unacceptable on our end," Burton said, as reported by Kenzo Fukuda of ClutchPoints. "Got to play better defense. Obviously, they're hitting good shots and getting good looks. I think we were sped up a little bit, but we cleaned it up in the other quarters defensively."

Golden State deserves credit for eventually tightening things up. The Dream scored just 34 points across the final three quarters, and the Valkyries managed to make the game somewhat competitive down the stretch.

But championship-caliber defense cannot disappear for an entire quarter, especially against an opponent facing elimination.

Gabby Williams pointed to ball pressure and physicality as areas Golden State must improve heading into Game 7.

"You set the tone with the physicality," Williams said. "I think when you punch first, when you are aggressive at the beginning and you try to be later, well, that's when fouls start getting called."

The Valkyries ultimately allowed Atlanta to dictate the pace early, and that proved costly.

While Golden State's defense deserves plenty of blame, its offense did little to help matters.

The Valkyries managed just 26 points in the first half, shooting a dismal 9-of-34 from the field. Atlanta's defensive pressure disrupted Golden State's offensive sets, forcing difficult attempts and preventing the Valkyries from establishing any consistent rhythm.

Williams finished with a game-high 26 points, but needed 22 field-goal attempts to get there, making just eight. Tiffany Hayes added 15 points, though Golden State struggled to find enough offensive production elsewhere to keep pace with Atlanta.

The Valkyries were particularly ineffective at attacking the basket early, allowing the Dream to control the game while Golden State settled into an inefficient offensive performance.

That changed somewhat in the second half, when Golden State became more aggressive getting to the rim and drawing fouls.

The Valkyries eventually cut Atlanta's lead to eight points late in the fourth quarter, an impressive turnaround considering they had trailed by as many as 25.

However, missed opportunities around the basket and the enormous early deficit left little room for error.

There is something to be said for Golden State's refusal to quit. The Valkyries could have folded after falling behind by 20 at halftime, but instead fought their way back into the contest.

Still, the late rally should not overshadow how poorly they executed offensively for much of the afternoon.

Golden State now has one final opportunity to secure its first WNBA championship Saturday.

Reporting by Charles Odum of The Associated Press was used in preparing this piece.

articles.title: The Hollow Day 8: Floor 8 Maze and the Sonaria Quest Guide - Core Roblox Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The Hollow Day 8 has you working your way through the movie theater's puzzle on Floor 8. You'll be completing a special puzzle at the end, and then
articles.body:
The Hollow Day 8 has you working your way through the movie theater's puzzle on Floor 8. You'll be completing a special puzzle at the end, and then you'll have a chance to complete another quest in the featured game for the day, Sonaria. Completing both tasks rewards you with a UGC reward, namely the Rotten Pumpkin and the Wings of Corrupted Jerry . In this guide, we'll be detailing a full walkthrough on how to complete the Floor 8 puzzle and how to complete the Sonaria quest in Roblox .

You can start the Hollow Day 8 maze puzzle by going to the movie theater's elevator and entering Floor 8. You'll need to navigate this to reach the Relic room. Like the other Relic rooms from the previous floors, the best way to reach it is by hugging the right side of the maze and taking as many rights as you can (avoiding the dead ends). The Relic room has always been on the right side, but the exact path of the maze does change.

You can see you've discovered the Relic room when you enter, and it has an altar to the left of the entrance. There are five different objects that you can pick up, but you can only pick up one at a time. You then need to bring them back to the maze and find the proper pedestals to put them on. The correct pedestal will have an outline of the object above it.

There's one for a bell, the potion, the lantern, the skull, and the candle. You'll need to return to the Relic room each time you place an object on a pedestal. After you've done this for all five items, you automatically get the Relic and can return to the elevator. If the monster catches you at any point during this portion, you'll need to start over from the beginning. Thankfully, the objects should not change positions, so long as you complete this maze on the same day.

The badge for completing the Floor 8 Maze automatically appears on your profile when you reach the top floor of the movie theater.

How to Complete the Sonaria Horror Escape Hollow Event

For the second part of Day 8, there's a quest for you to complete in Sonaria Horror Escape, called the Warden. You'll be making your way to the main lobby of this game and choosing the Warden mission. You can choose to do this yourself, but it is highly recommended to play with other players! You can complete it much faster alongside them, even if you're not in the same party.

You'll enter a match where you'll be choosing to play as Mylo the hunter, Vaelis the support, and Yoggy the lure.

You'll be working together through each floor to destroy the various infections that appear. You'll approach the infection sites, destroying the set amount that appear on that floor, before escaping to the door. You can do this by approaching the infection to attack it, and then rapidly clicking your attack button when the animation pops up. If you need help finding the infections, follow the red lights! These show you their exact positions.

There are enemies wandering around that you have to avoid if they get too close to you as you seek out the infections. Expect to pick up items along the way, and you should be using the items on your hot bar to increase your stamina, speed, and heal yourself.

You'll repeat this process for five floors, collecting items that you find and using your abilities. When you have other players helping you out, this part can happen pretty quickly!

After you reach round five, there's the final boss that you have to defeat the boss. Before you can get to them, there are infection sites that you need to destroy, lowering their shield.

With its shield down, the final boss appears, and you'll need to use Hollow Claws to throw at it. You need to be in range of the boss and use the item to damage it. You'll need to grab multiple of this item to do enough damage.

Once it reaches zero, you'll have defeated the boss and earned your reward! You can head back to the Hollow's lobby and receive your reward: Wings of Corrupted Jerry.
